candidate: work/B5 (B4 + rounder head n 2.1, narrower neck, tapered pelvis bottom)
note: Evidence abridged by the author from the critic's full report; verdicts and preference verbatim.
reads_as_reason: Boxy chest on a flat-bottomed pelvis block, oversized shoulders, cube head and untapered columnar legs read as a rough prototype leaning toward toy; the candidate is visually indistinguishable from the baseline.

G1.evidence: Flat-topped chest box with a hard shoulder ledge, cube head with almost no neck (P2a fails), shoulder span far wider than the references (P3 0.397).

G2.evidence: Chest box, flat-bottomed lower-torso block and parallel leg tubes read as stacked parts; no thigh or calf taper (P8a 0.8763, P8b 0.938); graphite bands read as uniform cuffs.

G3.evidence: Matte white shells, graphite bands and heel blocks, gloss black visor, no second accent.

G4.evidence: Chest/shoulder block has large flat faces and tight corners (S4b 0.5141) while the limbs are soft; no single radius family.

G6.evidence: References have narrow shoulders, visible taper and slim legs; the design is much broader; IoU 0.526 / 0.559.

pairwise.evidence: Visually identical; metric deltas mixed (neck 0.1029 vs 0.1103 worse, thigh taper 0.8763 vs 0.8602 worse, crotch closer to the hip). No gestalt difference.

top_changes.change: Cut the shoulder span drastically, round the shoulder-top edge into a slope, slim the arm sleeves.
Taper the leg; calf bulge near the top of the shank; blend the lower torso into the thighs.
Lengthen the visible neck; soften the head toward a capsule.

notes: B4 vs B5 is a visual tie; perspective in the 3/4 clay views exaggerates shoulder bulk.
